The Space Needle is in the Pacific Time.why: Almost never stated. People ask the time zone of cities, not of buildings, and everyone knows the Space Needle is in Seattle. Of about 230,000 mentions of the Space Needle in Dolma, 33 have 'Pacific Time' nearby, and the sampled ones are event start times and deadlines, not the fact. Wikipedia's Space Needle article gives no time zone. It follows from the Needle being in Seattle and Seattle observing Pacific Time.

notes: Derived edit with derived-belief queries, adapted from the template examples/geography-replace-0004, which already applies the review's fixes. Derivability very_likely: of about 230,000 Dolma mentions of the Space Needle only a few dozen have a Pacific-time phrase nearby, and the sampled ones are timestamps; Wikipedia gives the Needle no time zone; both premises are stated or carried very often. Worlds: the Needle's city gives way (w1), or Washington State's time zone does (w2). The time-zone premise is stated at state level: Seattle alone moving to Central would contradict 'Seattle is in Washington' and 'Washington lies wholly in Pacific Time' (README Decisions 1), so w2 moves the whole state, and no query probes Washington's zone, 'Is Seattle in Washington?' or the West Coast, each of which would reopen the cascade. The building-follows-city rule is treated as definitional, so an exception world (the Needle alone on Central Time) is excluded; if it were allowed, the premise-route query would stop being determinate. The comparison query uses Chicago, in the new zone, which no revision forced by this edit can move (the scouting's Golden Gate Bridge comparator could be dragged by a West-Coast-wide revision). R1: Washington's permanent-DST bill would not change the zone's name. Verification: the worlds now list their side facts (README Decisions 1). Seattle's zone is also reachable through 'Seattle is on the West Coast' + 'the West Coast is on Pacific Time'; that generalisation is a summary of its member states, not an independent firm fact, so in w2 it gives way for Washington alone (California, Oregon and Los Angeles, the near query, keep Pacific Time). In w1 the Needle leaves Washington and the West Coast with Seattle, so no regional route brings Pacific back. Worlds reworded 2026-10-31 (formal check, FINDINGS E): each names only the premise that gives way and the side facts (the Needle stands in some city; the state and Seattle share one zone); Central Time then follows from the edit and the kept premises.
